assertions.name: calibrates_against_the_corpus_electron_and_positron_values
assertions.source: electron = left trefoil T_(2,3), three POSITIVE crossings: E_cross = 3*q = 3.329935748 (pair-creation-energy.md says ~3.330); positron = mirror, three NEGATIVE: E_cross = -3/q = -2.702754852 (says ~-2.703). A reversed sign convention would swap these

assertions.name: gamma_gamma_crossing_energy_is_exactly_k_times_h
assertions.source: E_cross of a k-vertex gamma-gamma word = k*h exactly, k = 0..14 (each vertex is one positive and one negative crossing, q + (-1/q) = h). Mismatches: none

assertions.name: crossing_energy_is_blind_to_index_and_order
assertions.source: 3840 (permutation, index-assignment) pairs of a 5-vertex word -> 1 distinct value(s). E_cross is a sum over letters, so like the alternating character of #7295 it cannot see which vertex sits where

assertions.name: every_non_empty_gamma_gamma_word_is_repulsion_dominated
assertions.source: E_cross = k*h > 0 for every k >= 1 and every q > 1, since h = 0 only at q = [1]. def:crossing-energy reads a positive value as 'repulsion dominates' and a negative one as 'binding dominates', so NO gamma-gamma word is binding-dominated -- on any number of strands, at any q > 1. At q_0, h = 0.20906029879563931543

assertions.name: unconstrained_minimisation_is_degenerate_the_empty_word_wins
assertions.source: E_cross(empty word) = 0, against [('(v0 v1)^2', '0.836241195183'), ('(v0 v1)^4', '1.67248239037'), ('sporadic A', '2.09060298796'), ('sporadic B', '2.09060298796'), ('(v0 v1)^6', '2.50872358555')] for the five PSD-feasible words. So the UNCONSTRAINED minimum is the empty word -- the THIRD functional with that property, after the Markov trace and the LP objective (the latter proved degenerate by prop:operator-selection-lp). The demand constraint of knot-operator-selection-proof is the stated reason this may not be the last word, and it is NOT implemented here

assertions.name: ordering_among_non_empty_words_is_by_vertex_count_alone
assertions.source: sorted by E_cross: [('(v0 v1)^2', 4), ('(v0 v1)^4', 8), ('sporadic A', 10), ('sporadic B', 10), ('(v0 v1)^6', 12)] -- monotone in the vertex count, which is the whole content of E_cross = k*h. The two sporadic 10-vertex words TIE exactly, so even restricted to non-empty words this functional does not separate them

description: Crossing energy on gamma-gamma words. E_cross(k vertices) = k*h exactly -- a function of the vertex COUNT alone, blind to indices and order. Hence strictly POSITIVE for every non-empty word at every q > 1, and def:crossing-energy reads a positive value as repulsion-dominated: no gamma-gamma word is binding-dominated, on any number of strands. And minimising it is degenerate -- the empty word has E_cross = 0 -- making crossing energy the THIRD functional whose unconstrained optimum is the trivial answer. Does NOT implement knot-operator-selection-proof's demand constraint, which is the stated reason the unconstrained minimum may not be the last word. Calibrated against the corpus's own electron/positron values. Scope-(a).

data.definition: def:crossing-energy: E_cross(beta) = sum over crossings, +q for L_+, -1/q for L_-
findings: E_cross is a function of the vertex COUNT alone -- blind to index and order, like the alternating character and for the same reason
every non-empty gamma-gamma word is strictly POSITIVE hence repulsion-dominated, at every q > 1 and on any number of strands
unconstrained minimisation is degenerate: the empty word has E_cross = 0. Third functional with that property
even among non-empty words it does not separate the two sporadic 10-vertex candidates, which tie exactly
data.not_implemented: knot-operator-selection-proof's demand constraint <Phi, dem(K)>_F >= ||dem(K)||_F. Building dem(K) needs a state K, the Frobenius dual via G^-1, and a choice of which K the nucleon is -- the last being the question the arc is trying to settle, so wiring it here would be circular
